introduction: The study aims to describe lower secondary technology teachers' experiences of teaching digital models using digital tools. The research question asks how these teachers experience teaching digital models.
methodology: Twelve technology teachers, five males and seven females, were strategically chosen. Semi-structured interviews were chosen, guided by a question guide, lasting 35 to 60 minutes and recorded digitally. All were conducted by the first author in October 2018 and September 2019. A thematic analysis was used. The study was conducted in Swedish lower secondary schools.
theory: The study takes a phenomenological lifeworld approach as its ontological and epistemological basis. ‘Experience’ is its analytic concept.
results: Four themes were found: Enhancing and integrating other subjects; Visualizing technology to the pupils; Enabling digital modelling; and Preparing pupils for the future. The themes partly overlap. Teaching content and methods may differ. The synthesis indicates that teachers did not experience digital models as one single idea but as an amalgam of multiple ideas.
discussion: The overall result is that there is not one way to experience digital models, and therefore not one way to teach them. A conclusion is that discussion of this area needs to be more nuanced and specific to build a common knowledge base. Another topic for further research can be how digital models affect pupils' learning or interest in technology.

introduction.q: The aim of this study is to describe lower secondary technology teachers’ experiences of teaching digital models using digital tools.
How do lower secondary technology teachers experience the teaching of digital models?

a thematic analysis was used in this study

abstract_claims.q: The data were analyzed thematically and the results are four themes of experiencing the teaching of digital models, indicating that technology teachers teach with different aims and purposes; _Enhancing and integrating other subjects, Visualizing technology to the pupils, Enabling digital modelling,_ and _Preparing pupils for the future_.
Further, the results also indicate that the content and methods of teaching differ and that teachers did not experience digital models as one single idea but as an amalgam of multiple ideas.
These findings can be used as a basis for further research and development of teaching concerning digital models.

caveats.q: The aim of this study is not to distinguish between different teachers’ teaching, but to collect different experiences and analyze them thematically.
They all had formal teacher education, but not all in the technology subject.
However, investigating the teaching of digital models is limited to one particular reality, namely teachers’ experiences, formulated in the research question.
caveats.loc: Theory and method: Phenomenology of the lifeworld

caveats.q: The studied phenomenon is _teaching digital models_ in lower secondary technology education, and the results presented in this article are descriptive themes of teachers’ experiences.
Transcription constitutes a transformation from spoken language to written, and require interpretation by the person transcribing
However, the transcripts show that the teaching aspects from different themes sometimes were simultaneous described, which resulted in an overlapping of themes.
Sometimes two of the themes overlapped, sometimes three.
The excerpts are referred to a specific teacher, (Teacher 1) to (Teacher 12), but should be understood as a representation of the presented experience, or the teaching aspects within the theme.
However, the same teacher can have experiences referring to different themes, as an individual teacher can teach with different aims and purposes.
Above all, some of the interviewed teachers discuss mathematics and crafts as important subjects to enhance and integrate in relation to technology education.
Some teachers in this study experience that it is abstract to teach technical systems.
In the theme _Visualize technology to the pupils_, some interviewed teachers use ready-made digital models to show pupils technology that already exists.
Simulations give pupils a fast response and quick feedback on learning the specific teaching content, some interviewed teachers say.
Some teachers said in interviews that when programming, simulations on a screen alone are not enough for learning.
Sometimes, according to the interviewed teachers, pupils can create a physical model from their digital original.
What is designed is not important, since the learning content is to handle the software, some interviewed teachers say.
Teaching digital models is described mainly in two ways
The interviewed technology teachers have answered questions about _what_ and _how_, but the main focus in their responses has been _why_ they teach as they do
Teachers seem to try to strengthen the role of the subject by justifying their pedagogical choices and arguing why their teaching is important.
It seems more important for the interviewed teachers to justify their teaching than just to explain it.
It seems possible that these results explain why it becomes difficult to discuss teaching digital models
Could it be that technology teachers usually do not discuss the subject with colleagues?
Some technology teachers have to make individual decisions about their teaching.
Moreover, some teachers do not have organized conferences or shared arenas to discuss the technology subject with others

There are different experiences of teaching digital models, which can be interpreted as an indication that there is no consensus regarding teaching content or methods of teaching digital models, the progression of the teaching content, or the levels of knowledge that pupils are supposed to acquire.
The aim and purpose of teaching digital models, the four themes, seem more important than the specific content.
but there is a lack of reflection concerning the choice of content and method.
Therefore, to get a more holistic view of technology education, aspects of creating and designing in digital environments need to be elaborated on in future studies.

overclaims.body: The synthesis shows that teaching digital models is not centered on only one objective, and teaching content and methods may differ, but also overlap between the various aims and purposes.
